## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode. ---AGENTS--- # OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review. Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests. ## Wiki index - [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md) - [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md) - [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md) - [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md) - [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md) - [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md) ## Main project file The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml). Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md) aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job. Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue. Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use the `codex://threads/` URL format. When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days. ## OpenCode GitHub Actions To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user. Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation. The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward. When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status. Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`, which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit. Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account. Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only. Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota. Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound. Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries. Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save. Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker. To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`, then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` to discover the host and port and SSH with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper. When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when live log evidence can be collected. For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ``` The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from `_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while inspecting the runner. ## Mac SSH access The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as: ```sh ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running. ## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub ``` For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and use the same key: ```sh ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \ -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \ -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \ -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never print secrets while inspecting a worker. ---README---
# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a polished 3D single-player Napoleonic Wars skirmish game in Three.js with realistic procedural animations and ragdolls.
- The game is titled “Fields of Honour — Waterloo 1815” and runs in the browser.

## Requirements
- 3D Napoleonic wars skirmish, single-player.
- Realistic animations and ragdolls.
- User did not state explicit platform constraints beyond the game concept.
- Repository/browser instructions require mobile support, usable touch controls, and browser screenshot verification.

## Decisions
- Use Vite + Three.js with procedural assets, no external model downloads.
- Third-person over-shoulder rifleman gameplay: WASD movement, mouse aim/fire, R reload, C crouch, F bayonet.
- British 95th Rifles vs French line infantry, three waves defending an orchard near La Haye Sainte.
- Procedural soldier rigs with merged geometry, walking/aiming/reload/melee animation, Verlet-style ragdolls, dropped muskets.
- Add synthesized WebAudio musket/cannon sounds, smoke/particle effects, cannonballs, postprocessing, HUD, start/pause/end screens.
- Use a read-only debug handle at `window.__fieldsOfHonour` for browser testing.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created Vite project, installed `three`, `@fontsource/cinzel`, `@fontsource/barlow-condensed`, `@fontsource/cormorant-garamond`.
- Built `index.html`, `src/style.css`, `src/utils.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/effects.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/soldier.js`, `src/main.js`.
- `npm run build` succeeds.
- Browser loads with no page errors after fixes.
- Start screen, gameplay HUD, battlefield, soldiers, flags, cannon, grass, trees, farmhouse, and postprocessing render.
- Fixed missing `createDistantCrowd` function reference by renaming call to `makeDistantCrowd`.
- Fixed enemy AI bug where `ready` enemies automatically entered reload instead of waiting for volley.
- Reduced grass height/density, moved player/allies/enemies closer, raised/pulled back camera, reduced fog, darkened sky, improved tree shapes, moved orchard/farmhouse/tree positions.
- Added favicon data URI.
- Added `window.__fieldsOfHonour` debug handle.

### Active
- Improving visual fidelity and screenshot quality.
- Just added `makeGroundTexture()` and `makeShadowTexture()` in `src/utils.js`.
- Added ground texture to terrain material in `src/world.js`.
- Added imports for `makeShadowTexture` and a shared `shadowMaterial` in `src/soldier.js`; the shadow plane itself has **not yet been added** to the soldier rig.

### Blocked

326:     this.constraints = []
327:     for (const [a, b, stiffness] of pairs) {

329:       const pb = this.parts[b]
330:       const len = Math.hypot(pa.x - pb.x, pa.y - pb.y, pa.z - pb.z)
331:       this.constraints.push({ a: pa, b: pb, len, stiffness })

333:     const impulse = dir.clone().normalize().multiplyScalar(force)

335:       head: 1.5, chest: 1.2, hips: 0.9, shoulderL: 0.8, shoulderR: 0.8,
336:       handL: 0.5, handR: 0.5, hipL: 0.7, hipR: 0.7, kneeL: 0.5, kneeR: 0.5,
337:     }
338:     for (const part of Object.values(this.parts)) {
339:       const w = weights[part.name] || 0.4

341:       part.py -= impulse.y * w - rand(0.25, 1.1) * (part.name === 'head' ? 1 : 0.55)

343:       if (part.name === 'head' || part.name === 'chest') {
344:         part.px -= rand(-1.5, 1.5)
345:         part.pz -= rand(-1.5, 1.5)
346:       }

358:   simulate(dt) {
359:     if (this.settled) return
360:     this.accum = Math.min(this.accum + dt, 0.1)
361:     const step = 1 / 60
362:     let maxV = 0
363:     while (this.accum >= step) {
364:       this.accum -= step
365:       this.time += step
366:       for (const p of Object.values(this.parts)) {
367:         const vx = (p.x - p.px) * 0.994
368:         const vy = (p.y - p.py) * 0.994
369:         const vz = (p.z - p.pz) * 0.994
370:         p.px = p.x
371:         p.py = p.y
372:         p.pz = p.z
373:         p.x += vx
374:         p.y += vy - 9.2 * step * step
375:         p.z += vz
376:         if (p.y < p.radius) {
377:           p.y = p.radius
378:           p.px = p.x - vx * 0.62
379:           p.pz = p.z - vz * 0.62
380:           p.py = p.y
381:         }
382:         maxV = Math.max(maxV, Math.abs(vx) + Math.abs(vy) + Math.abs(vz))
383:       }
384:       for (let iter = 0; iter < 5; iter++) {
385:         for (const c of this.constraints) {
386:           const a = c.a
387:           const b = c.b
388:           let dx = b.x - a.x
389:           let dy = b.y - a.y
390:           let dz = b.z - a.z
391:           const d = Math.hypot(dx, dy, dz) || 0.0001
392:           const diff = (d - c.len) / d
393:           const total = a.mass + b.mass
394:           const k = c.stiffness * diff
395:           a.x += dx * k * (b.mass / total)
396:           a.y += dy * k * (b.mass / total)
397:           a.z += dz * k * (b.mass / total)
398:           b.x -= dx * k * (a.mass / total)
399:           b.y -= dy * k * (a.mass / total)
400:           b.z -= dz * k * (a.mass / total)
401:         }
402:       }
403:     }
404:     if (maxV < 0.008) this.sleep += dt
405:     else this.sleep = 0
406:     if (this.sleep > 2.5 || this.time > 18) this.settled = true
407:   }

411: function createFences(scene) {
412:   const wood = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ map: makeWoodTexture(), roughness: 1, color: 0x7d6345 })
413:   const parts = []
414:   function segment(x1, z1, x2, z2, yOff = 0) {
415:     const dx = x2 - x1
416:     const dz = z2 - z1
417:     const len = Math.hypot(dx, dz)
418:     const angle = Math.atan2(dx, dz)
419:     const count = Math.max(2, Math.round(len / 2.5))
420:     for (let i = 0; i <= count; i++) {
421:       const t = i / count
422:       const x = x1 + dx * t
423:       const z = z1 + dz * t
424:       const y = terrainHeight(x, z) + 0.55
425:       const g = new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.14, 1.2, 0.14)
426:       g.applyMatrix4(new THREE.Matrix4().compose(
427:         new THREE.Vector3(x, y + yOff, z),
428:         new THREE.Quaternion().setFromEuler(new THREE.Euler(rand(-0.04, 0.04), angle, rand(-0.04, 0.04))),
429:         new THREE.Vector3(1, 1, 1)
430:       ))
431:       parts.push(g)
432:     }
433:     for (let r = 0; r < 3; r++) {
434:       const g = new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.1, 0.13, len)
435:       const midX = (x1 + x2) / 2
436:       const midZ = (z1 + z2) / 2
437:       const y = terrainHeight(midX, midZ) + 0.35 + r * 0.34 + yOff
438:       g.applyMatrix4(new THREE.Matrix4().compose(
439:         new THREE.Vector3(midX, y, midZ),
440:         new THREE.Quaternion().setFromEuler(new THREE.Euler(0, angle, 0)),
441:         new THREE.Vector3(1, 1, 1)
442:       ))
443:       parts.push(g)
444:     }
445:   }
446:   segment(-18, -3.5, -9.5, -3.1)
447:   segment(9.5, -3.1, 18, -3.8)
448:   segment(-19, 4.5, -12, 4.5)
449:   segment(12, 4.2, 20, 4.4)
450:   segment(18, 2, 18, -14)
451:   segment(-21, 2, -21, -15)
452:   const merged = mergeGeometries(parts)
453:   const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(merged, wood)
454:   mesh.castShadow = true
455:   mesh.receiveShadow = true
456:   scene.add(mesh)
457: }

616: export class World {
617:   constructor(scene) {
618:     this.scene = scene
619:     this.colliders = []
620:     this.cannons = []
621:     this.time = 0
622:     this.sky = makeSky(scene)
623:     makeTerrain(scene)
624:     const wind = makeGrass(scene)
625:     this.grassShader = wind.shaderRef
626:     this.wheatShader = wind.wheatShaderRef
627:     createDistantHills(scene)
628:     createTreeLine(scene)
629:     createOrchard(scene)
630:     createFarmhouse(scene)
631:     createBarn(scene)
632:     createFences(scene)
633:     makeDistantCrowd(scene)
634:     this.flags = createFlags(scene)
635:     this.cannons.push(createCannon(scene, -14.5, 1.8, Math.PI + 0.08))
636:     this.cannons.push(createCannon(scene, 18, -47, 0.12))
637: 
638:     // Collision volumes for the large structures and trunks.
639:     this.colliders.push({ type: 'box', x: -30, z: -8, hx: 5.9, hz: 3.9, rot: 0.14 })
640:     this.colliders.push({ type: 'box', x: 33, z: -20, hx: 4.8, hz: 3.3, rot: -0.2 })
641:     this.colliders.push({ type: 'circle', x: -25, z: 10, r: 0.6 })
642:     this.colliders.push({ type: 'circle', x: -14, z: -13, r: 0.45 })
643:     this.colliders.push({ type: 'circle', x: 27, z: -9, r: 0.5 })
644:     for (let row = 0; row < 4; row++) {
645:       for (let col = 0; col < 4; col++) {
646:         this.colliders.push({ type: 'circle', x: 22 + row * 4.7, z: 4 - col * 4.9, r: 0.38 })
647:       }
648:     }
649: 
650:     // Stone wall in front of the allied line, broken by a gate.
651:     this.colliders.push({ type: 'box', x: -13, z: -3.4, hx: 4.6, hz: 0.55, rot: 0 })
652:     this.colliders.push({ type: 'box', x: 13, z: -3.4, hx: 4.6, hz: 0.55, rot: 0 })
653:   }
654: 
655:   update(dt, time) {
656:     this.time = time
657:     if (this.grassShader.value) this.grassShader.value.uniforms.uTime.value = time
658:     if (this.wheatShader.value) this.wheatShader.value.uniforms.uTime.value = time
659:     this.sky.uniforms.uTime.value = time
660: 
661:     for (const f of this.flags) {
662:       const pos = f.mesh.geometry.attributes.position
663:       const arr = pos.array
664:       for (let i = 0; i < pos.count; i++) {
665:         const x = f.basePositions[i * 3]
666:         const y = f.basePositions[i * 3 + 1]
667:         const u = x / (1.7 * f.scale)
668:         const wave = Math.sin(x * 4.2 - time * 5.2 + f.phase) * 0.13 + Math.sin(x * 8.1 - time * 8.4 + f.phase) * 0.045
669:         arr[i * 3 + 2] = wave * u * f.scale
670:         arr[i * 3 + 1] = y + Math.sin(x * 3.1 - time * 4.1 + f.phase) * 0.045 * u * f.scale
671:       }
672:       pos.needsUpdate = true
673:       f.mesh.geometry.computeVertexNormals()
674:     }
675: 
676:     for (const c of this.cannons) {
677:       if (c.recoil > 0) {
678:         c.recoil = Math.max(0, c.recoil - dt * 1.9)
679:         const kick = Math.sin(Math.min(1, c.recoil) * Math.PI) * 0.42
680:         c.barrel.position.z = c.baseZ - kick
681:         c.barrel.rotation.x = -kick * 0.14
682:       } else {
683:         c.barrel.position.z = c.baseZ
684:         c.barrel.rotation.x = 0
685:       }
686:     }
687:   }
688: 
689:   cannonMuzzle(cannon) {
690:     return cannon.muzzle.getWorldPosition(new THREE.Vector3())
691:   }
692: 
693:   fireCannon(cannon) {
694:     cannon.recoil = 1
695:   }
696:

```
else if (!game.started) { ... }
else if (!game.paused) { ... } // paused → do nothing
```
Actually when paused, skip all simulation, but still render and update effects? Effects update dt continues, so smoke drifts while paused. Should pause effects too? Ideally freeze. World flags/sky can continue for atmosphere; fine. But units should freeze. Let's modify:
```
} else if (!game.paused) {
  updateAllies(dt*0.2)...
}
```
But when game.over true and !paused, updateGame handles over and returns, so else doesn't run. Fine.

When paused, updateCamera still runs and might drift? updateCamera uses player state and dt, but camera position lerps to desired, no input; fine. HUD updates only if started (yes, updateHUD runs even when paused) but timers tick down; pause screen overlays. Not critical.

Wait, there's a logic issue: `else if (!game.paused)` after `else if (!game.started)` — if started and paused, neither branch runs. If started and not paused but game.over? updateGame is called (game.started && !game.paused) regardless of game.over, and updateGame handles over. So the final else-if is unreachable except when game.started && paused? Actually the chain:
1. if (started && !paused) → covers started not paused, including over.
2. else if (!started) → not started.
3. else if (!paused) → started && paused && !paused = impossible.
So the last branch is dead code. That's fine; remove it. The intent was for game.over, but updateGame handles it. So simplify:
```
if (started && !paused) updateGame
else if (!started) tableau
```
Paused does nothing. Let's clean up.
